A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same interaction-layer and ACDA research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably, including v1 Appendix F, which becomes v2 Appendix H.

before.justification: V1 reports original MuJoCo experiments comparing ACDA with baselines, plus noise-sensitivity and adaptation ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original WiFi-delay measurements, simulation results using those measurements, robustness experiments, and execution-time measurements.

M1.justification: The principal interaction layer, memorized-action heuristic, latent model, and training objectives are retained. Appendix G.3 adds an evaluated packet-skipping adaptation that generates actions from selected observations and makes memorized-action prediction account for skipped packets.

E1.justification: The same five MuJoCo tasks remain, but v2 extends the three simulated delay processes with library and office WiFi recordings replayed in simulation. Appendix F additionally evaluates independent Poisson(3) and DCAC WiFi delays, substantially broadening the delay conditions tested.

E2.justification: Dreamer, implemented using Dreamerv3, and DCAC join the existing comparisons in Section 5 and Appendix E.1. DCAC was explicitly excluded in v1. BPQL with the MDA policy was already evaluated in v1 and is retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds noise sweeps, floor/ceiling average-delay CDA settings, measured-trace replay with 99th-percentile delay bounds, and observation-skipping rates. The original million-step training and ten-trajectory evaluation schedule remains. The new WiFi low-CDA captions specify h=4 in Figures 28–29, whereas Table 8 specifies 1, leaving that particular setting inconsistent.

E4.justification: V2 retains the original MDA and low-CDA ablations while substantially extending noise sensitivity, including comparisons across 0–25% noise. It adds average-delay CDA sensitivity, tests violations of temporal correlation, evaluates packet skipping, and analyzes computational costs in Appendices B.2, E.4, F, and G.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 newly discloses VDPO's fixed environment-reset seed and explains zero standard deviations in noiseless evaluations. Both versions retain ten-trajectory evaluations and standard-deviation reporting; v2 does not add reported repetitions across independent training seeds or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive WiFi, independent-delay, noise, timing, and packet-skipping results. Original synthetic-delay benchmark and ablation scores are retained. Existing noise-study values also change: BPQL's HalfCheetah return at delay 3 without noise changes from 7839.43 in v1 Figure 9 to 8159.28 in v2 Table 3.

T1.justification: The POMDP formalization, model objective, and continuous-time mathematics are retained. Appendix G adds limited computational-cost reasoning, including sequential work proportional to h+L and the packet-generation time derivation in Equation 35. No convergence proof is added.

C1.justification: The interaction-layer and ACDA contributions remain central. The abstract and introduction extend the performance claims to measured WiFi delays and competitors handling unobservable random delays, and the introduction now acknowledges DCAC's use of hindsight delay information.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of missing convergence guarantees, performance under independent delays, computational bottlenecks, bandwidth requirements, and delays outside the interaction layer. Section 5 also qualifies superiority under alternative CDA settings, stating that ACDA leads in 15 of 25 benchmarks when all evaluated configurations are considered.

D1.justification: V2 documents WiFi collection using 100000 packets, 8 ms intervals, and 12000-byte payloads; explicitly specifies prediction-length and buffer-horizon choices; and explains Dreamer/DCAC integration and runtime. It also adds an explicit code-archive access link. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's existing architecture and hyperparameter details.

R1.justification: V1 characterizes DCAC as requiring observable delays; v2 recognizes its handling of unobservable delays and shifts the distinction toward control over action execution. Related-work positioning also expands to offline delayed RL, action chunking, and measured network-delay correlation, substantially revising the novelty context.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the original exposition remain. V2 polishes language, reorganizes related-work paragraphs, clarifies delay and clock terminology, and updates appendix navigation. The continuous-time appendix moves from F to H without a substantive rewrite.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format. Figure 2 is substantially redrawn, Table 1 changes its rows and displayed delay conditions, and numerous new experimental displays are added. Appendix E.5 also consolidates previously displayed results into comparison tables.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important comparison gap by revising its characterization of DCAC and actually evaluating it alongside Dreamer. Measured WiFi-delay replay and tests of noise, delay assumptions, independence, and computational constraints substantially strengthen the evidence and clarify applicability. Reproducibility also improves. Some overstatement remains: the introduction's 'all except one' claim overlooks the new Office/Hopper exception in Table 14, but this does not outweigh the substantial gains.
